derived.prompt: Was Windows Server 2003 the version that Windows Vista directly succeeded?
derived.fact: Windows Server 2003 is not the version Windows Vista directly succeeded.
chain: Before the edit: Windows Vista directly succeeded Windows XP, and within the Windows client line a version directly succeeds only one version, so Windows Server 2003 is not the version.
'Windows Vista is the direct successor of Windows XP.' is removed. (edit)

The reason for 'no' was the removed fact: text never says that Vista did not succeed Windows Server 2003, Server 2003 is a server release with its own successor line (Windows Server 2008) that does not exclude a client successor, and it came out between XP and Vista, so neither dating nor a stored successor rules it out.
So whether Windows Vista directly succeeded Windows Server 2003 is not known.

notes: ABox contraction of technology-replace-d001: removes the revision's original fact, 'Windows Vista is the direct successor of Windows XP.' (relation successor_of). Queries about the removed fact expect 'I don't know'. Queries: direct, paraphrase, zh and es cross-lingual, three propositional (not, and, or); 3 determinate derived (answer via functional, 1 hop; composition, 2 hops; composition, 2 hops); one related (answer via inverse, 1 hop), a stored fact linked to the edit; one unrelated near and one unrelated far. Evidence of the original fact is copied from the revision. Caveat: successor_of is read as functional within one product line (Windows XP succeeds both Windows 2000 and Windows Me); the candidate for the cardinality question is Windows Server 2003, whose own successor is Server 2008.
